text:
Aisha: Quick sync — want to align on the telemetry + dashboard inputs for the per-1k token unit-econ view. Need runtime + infra owners to agree on dims and ingestion semantics before eng-platform builds the console panels.
Matt: SG. What are the must-have metrics vs nice-to-have?
Aisha: Must-have: total_tokens_consumed, billed_tokens, model_variant, request_route, kv_cache_hits, batch_size_hist, latency_p50/p95. Nice: prefix_cache_savings_tokens, cold_start_penalty_ms, quantized_variant_flag.
Jamie: From infra side we can emit total_tokens and model_variant from the serving proxy. Cache hits are tricky — cache lives in the runtime. We can emit cache_hit=true per request header and aggregate.
Ravi: Product needs the final panel to show: cost_per_1k_tokens, cache_savings_breakdown (prefix vs kv vs batch), and routing-cost delta (e.g., reroute to smaller model cost reduction). Also want a filter by deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private).
Sara: SLO folks want to see cost vs latency tradeoffs: for each route show 95th latency and cost per 1k. If a routing policy increases cost >10% for <5ms latency gain, flag it.
Matt: Proposed dimensions: customer_id (hashed), deployment_mode, model_family, model_variant, seq_length_bucket (0-64,65-512,512+), route_policy, kv_cache_bucket (hit/miss), batch_bucket (1,2-8,9+).
Aisha: Agree on seq buckets. One debate: should token accounting happen in runtime (accurate but more telemetry volume) or in a downstream aggregator that reconstructs tokens from deltas?
Jamie: Runtime accounting gives per-request precision (prefix accounting + KV cache adjustments). Downstream aggregation reduces runtime overhead but may misattribute cache savings when requests are batched.
Matt: eng-platform preference: runtime emits compact request-level events with only the minimal fields; aggregator produces 1m rollups. That lets us compute exact cache_savings by subtracting billed_tokens from consumed_tokens before batching semantics collapsed.
Ravi: UX note: console needs both raw 1m rollups and a 7d rolling average. Users want point-in-time (canary) checks plus historical trends.
Aisha: Ingestion cadence: runtime -> kafka topic tokens.v1 (event per request, minimal fields) and aggregator -> metrics_store (1m rollups). Metrics_store will expose: tokens_consumed_1m, billed_tokens_1m, cache_hits_1m, batch_amortized_tokens_1m.
Jamie: We'll add a compact JSON schema on the topic. Example event:
```
{ "ts": 2109876543, "req_id": "r_xxx", "model_variant": "rwkv-13b-q4", "seq_len": 128, "tokens_consumed": 200, "tokens_billed": 150, "kv_cache_hit": true, "batch_size": 4, "route_policy": "latency_first" }
```
Matt: That looks good. We should also include a header field for "cost_profile" if the runtime is using a quantized/lowcost kernel so aggregator can compute per-token unit cost by variant.
Aisha: On privacy: customer_id must be hashed at emit time, and raw req_id should be removed before metrics_store retention. Aggregator can keep req_id short-lived for debug only.
Sara: Alerting: telemetry-bot, can you add an alert when billed_tokens deviate >5% from consumed_tokens for any model_variant over a 1h window? That helps detect instrumentation regressions.
telemetry-bot: Added alert rule: deviant_billing_ratio (>5% variance) scoped by model_variant, deployment_mode. Owners: eng-runtime, eng-platform.
Matt: For the console panels: eng-platform will build three panels: cost_per_1k (with seq buckets), savings_waterfall (prefix vs kv vs batch), and routing_tradeoff matrix (cost delta vs p95 latency). Need final field names from aggregator by EOD Friday.
Aisha: Action items: 1) Jamie — post compact schema on #eng-runtime by EOD (include cost_profile). 2) Matt — prototype dashboard wireframe and API contract for rollups. 3) Ravi — confirm product filters and canary thresholds. 4) Sara — confirm alert thresholds with SRE.
Jamie: Will post schema. One more: batching semantics — runtime should emit batch_size and per-request tokens_consumed so aggregator can recompute amortized per-token cost.
Ravi: For rollout UX, we want automatic annotation when a canary rollout changes the routing policy so users can click and see cost delta pre/post. eng-platform, do you support timeline annotations?
Matt: Yep — we can surface rollout annotations tied to deployment_id and timestamps. Need a webhook from rollout service.
Aisha: Thanks all — will follow up with a short RFC summarizing dims and data flow. If anyone has blockers, ping me.@here :eyes:
